answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Matching. Each identity’s action sequence is scored per epoch against its own prior distribution; a large divergence flags the identity. To persist, an attacker must let each synthetic agent wander through low-value actions long enough to build a plausible history, delaying payoff by multiple epochs. A garden of dormant identities still fails, since each must accrue genuine variance at real cost. Only identities whose trajectory stays coherent yield a pearl of trust weight.
